Photorealistic documentary workplace photography for Dutch vocational teenagers. Authentic ordinary Dutch workplaces, adult workers, natural daylight, believable tools and hands. NO school, classroom, cartoons, captions, borders, watermarks, logos, legible text, numbers, prices, times, diagrams or maths. This is a work conversation photo, never an instruction diagram. Main material and work action must be visually clear. Avoid exaggerated posing or glossy advertising. Create ONE contact sheet with EXACTLY 3 equal columns and 4 equal rows, no gaps, no borders. Canvas 1536 by 1024, each cell a separate wide 2:1 scene, camera framing contained completely inside its cell. Reading order left to right then next row. The twelve separate scenes are:
1. An adult shop assistant in a modest Dutch household shop attaches a blank-looking shelf-edge price card below a row of ordinary unbranded goods. Hands, label holder and goods clearly visible, no readable price or text.
2. An adult grocery shop assistant opens a cardboard delivery case containing unbranded sealed biscuit boxes and places one box on a grocery shelf. The biscuit boxes have small biscuit pictures but no writing.
3. A shop assistant at a small Dutch gift-shop counter puts an ordinary gift item in a plain kraft paper gift bag, several unused paper gift bags nearby, authentic hands and neutral counter.
4. A grocery shop assistant neatly places unbranded sealed coffee packets on a shelf, natural everyday supermarket surroundings. Small coffee-bean graphics identify coffee, absolutely no readable branding or writing.
5. At a Dutch online-retail packing bench an employee slides a neatly folded plain T-shirt into a grey plastic shipping mailer and prepares the self-adhesive flap. A stack of unused empty grey mailers is visible. No address labels.
6. A shop employee clips a plain plastic front strip onto the edge of a small display shelf. Shelf fixings and hands clearly visible, nearby everyday retail goods. The strip contains no writing or digits.
7. A support worker in an ordinary Dutch residential care home folds simple napkins and puts them next to cups and plates on a homely dining table. No residents or medical equipment visible.
8. A care-home support worker prepares a mug of tea in a small homely staff kitchenette. A tea bag with plain string and several unbranded tea bags in a compartment tray are clearly visible. No printed tea labels.
9. A care-home support worker puts a stack of clean folded towels in a low wooden storage cupboard with open doors. Full cupboard, worker hands and towels visible in a calm care-home corridor.
10. In a modest Dutch cafe a waiter offers a closed plain menu folder to an adult guest seated at a tidy table. Several similar closed menu folders at the service point. No readable lettering.
11. An adult cafe employee puts a glass of water on a plain cork drinks coaster at a wooden cafe table, a short stack of additional cork coasters nearby, clear professional serving gesture.
12. A restaurant employee neatly folds cloth napkins beside a stack of clean plates while preparing a table before service. Ordinary modern Dutch restaurant, natural light, no glamour.
